headline: D-Wave announced a joint project with Nasdaq Verafin to test whether quantum computing can help spot financial crime.
score_reason: Pool score 5 lowered by 2: the announcement dates from 3 Aug 2026 and the page was re-dated; it is an early proof-of-concept with no results.
importance_line: Banks and other financial firms might eventually get better tools against fraud and money laundering, but this is only a first test with no results reported, and it was announced in August.
summary: Stocktwits reports that D-Wave, a quantum computing company known for its annealing machines (a type built to find good answers to complex optimisation problems), said it will work with Nasdaq Verafin, a financial-crime detection software provider used by more than 2,800 financial institutions, on a proof-of-concept test of quantum-hybrid methods for spotting fraud, scams and money laundering. It could grow into pilot applications if the first test succeeds, but no results are reported; the announcement dates from 3 Aug 2026, so this is older news.
notes: Older news re-dated (feed date 11 Oct 2026; event 3 Aug 2026, dated from Google News listings of other outlets, not from the article text).
